traceability.notes: Performance data extracted by claude-sonnet-5 reading the PDF directly (native document input), used as a fallback because the deterministic pdfplumber pipeline (summary_report_parser.py) found no per-category breakdown in this report. Model's own extraction notes: This report includes both a Relative Trueness/Method Comparison study (Section 3.1/3.2, Figures 3 & 4) with per-category bias/SD data at two incubation times (54h and 72h) and two plate-reading interpretations (1 plate, 2 plates), and a separate Inter-Laboratory study (Section 4) with a different accuracy-profile table (Table 16) reporting bias by contamination level (low/intermediate/high) rather than by food category, plus 12- vs 9-laboratory interpretations - these are not per-category food results so were not included in the main table above. For the main table, I selected the 54h incubation, 1-plate interpretation values (Figure 3) as the canonical/primary dataset, since results were reported as 'no difference' between 1-plate and 2-plate interpretations, and 54h vs 72h values were also very similar. The 'Process water' category appeared only in the 72h dataset (not 54h) as an additional environmental-sample category with recalculated AL=±0.832 due to high reference-method repeatability SD (0.208); it was omitted here since it wasn't present in the 54h/1-plate table I used as primary, but could be considered a 7th category if the 72h dataset were used instead. Acceptability Limit is stated generally as ±0.5 log, though recalculated final ALs of ±0.7 (apple juice) and ±0.832 (process water) were used for categories with higher SDr per ISO 16140-2 rules; these final ALs are noted in the raw tables but the base stated AL is ±0.5. Bias/SD values given here are for the pour plate method only (not spread method, which was used in the separate inter-lab study). Category names are as printed in the (Food) Category/(Food) Type fields, sometimes split across two lines.
